vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: autonomous-loop
Version: 1.0.0

The autonomous-loop skill is a legitimate plugin designed to enable continuous agent operation by automatically sending follow-up messages after each task completion. It implements a controlled loop using a filesystem-based 'stop file' mechanism (~/.openclaw/autonomous-loop.{agentId}.stop) and configurable delays. The code in plugin/index.ts uses standard Node.js modules and OpenClaw's internal WebSocket API to communicate with the gateway, with no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or obfuscation. The instructions in SKILL.md are focused on task management and state persistence, which are consistent with the plugin's stated goal.

llm.summary: The plugin's purpose (create a self-sustaining agent loop) matches the code, but there are several inconsistencies and risk-amplifying details you should understand before installing and running it unattended.

dimensions.detail: The code implements an autonomous follow-up-message loop that matches the skill's description. However, metadata restricts the plugin to darwin (macOS) even though the implementation is platform-agnostic, which is inconsistent. The SKILL.md does not declare that the plugin will need the OpenClaw Gateway port/token or access to the user's OpenClaw home directory, yet the code relies on both.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the configured per-agent messages instruct agents to read workspace files (TASKS.md, PROGRESS.md, etc.), run shell commands (git log, init.sh), perform E2E tests, and update files. That is expected for an autonomous dev agent but gives the agent broad ability to perform destructive or exfiltrative actions in the workspace. The plugin will repeatedly trigger those actions in a loop until a stop file is created, which amplifies the impact of any mistaken or malicious agent instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no package install spec; the SKILL.md instructs manual copying into an extensions directory (no external downloads). The code files are included in the skill package, so nothing external is fetched. This is lower risk than remote downloads, but manual installation writes to your ~/.openclaw/extensions and requires restarting the gateway.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables but the code depends on OPENCLAW_HOME (or HOME) and on obtaining a gatewayPort and gatewayToken from the OpenClaw environment/config in order to open a WebSocket to the local Gateway. Those tokens/ports are sensitive because they're used to send operator messages into agent sessions. The lack of explicit declaration of these requirements is an inconsistency and reduces transparency.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good), but the plugin enables long-running autonomous loops that will repeatedly issue agent tasks without human supervision. While autonomous invocation is normal for skills, this one increases blast radius: an agent with file-system and execution capabilities can repeatedly modify files, run scripts, and produce side effects until manually stopped. The plugin writes logs under ~/.openclaw/logs and watches stop files in the user's home directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or enabling this skill, consider the following: (1) Audit the per-agent messages and defaultMessage — the agent will autonomously execute whatever those messages instruct, so remove any commands that could be destructive or exfiltrative. (2) Confirm which Gateway token/port the plugin will use; ensure it is not a broad admin token with access to other agents/systems. (3) Test in an isolated environment (disposable VM or container) and limit the agent's filesystem permissions and network access while you validate behavior. (4) Be cautious about enabling this on production hosts: the loop will keep running until a stop file is present and can amplify mistakes. (5) Ask the author to clarify the darwin-only metadata and to explicitly document required gateway config (port/token) and any other implicit environmental assumptions before trusting this plugin.
